{{Short description|Theorem of mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Cohen–Hewitt factorization theorem''' states that if <math> V </math> is a [[left module]] over a [[Banach algebra]] <math> B </math> with a left approximate unit <math> (u_{i})_{i \in I} </math>, then an element <math> v </math> of <math> V </math> can be factorized as a product <math> v = b w </math> (for some <math> b \in B </math> and <math> w \in V </math>) whenever <math> \displaystyle \lim_{i \in I} u_{i} v = v </math>. The theorem was introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Paul Cohen (mathematician)|last=Cohen|first=Paul|year=1959}} and {{harvs|txt|last=Hewitt|first=Edwin|authorlink=Edwin Hewitt|year=1964}}.
